analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a respectable industrials business — abrasives, ceramics, electrominerals — but it's priced at 74x earnings despite single-digit profit growth, making the PEG ratio an alarming ~9.8. The story weakens dramatically in FY25: net profit collapsed 37% from ₹476 Cr to ₹299 Cr while revenue barely moved from ₹4,702 to ₹4,894 Cr.
key_strengths: Virtually debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.08) with growing equity base from ₹1,858 Cr to ₹3,745 Cr over 5 years
Diversified business across surface engineering, technical ceramics, and electrominerals — not a single-product play
Consistent OCF positive across all 5 years; long operating history since 1954 with institutional backing (DII at 30%)
key_risks: Net profit CAGR of only 7.6% over 9 years — this is a slow grower wearing a fast-grower price tag at P/E 74x
FY25 net profit crashed 37% YoY (₹476→₹299 Cr) with FCF collapsing to just ₹28 Cr — the growth story is visibly fracturing
Operating margin of only 7.43% despite 57% gross margin signals massive operational cost bloat or subsidiary drag
red_flags: Other income swung from +₹118 Cr (FY24) to -₹23 Cr (FY25) — a ₹141 Cr hit that hammered net profits and needs explanation
P/E of 74.2 on ~7.6% historical earnings growth gives PEG of ~9.8 — one of the worst PEG ratios by Lynch standards
Revenue growth has been stagnant the last two years (₹4,654→₹4,702→₹4,894 Cr) — the business may be hitting a ceiling
analysis.detailed_analysis: CARBORUNIV is what Lynch would call a stalwart masquerading as a growth stock. The business — abrasives, industrial ceramics, electrominerals — is solid and defensible, but 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.8% and profit CAGR of 7.6% simply don't justify a 74x earnings multiple. With a PEG of nearly 10, you're paying extraordinary growth-stock prices for below-average growth — a deal Lynch would never make. The FY25 numbers are genuinely alarming: net profit dropped from ₹476 Cr to ₹299 Cr despite flat revenue, other income turned sharply negative, and free cash flow nearly vanished at just ₹28 Cr. Something broke in FY25 and management hasn't demonstrated it's a one-off. Until the earnings story clarifies and the valuation corrects meaningfully, this is a business to watch, not own.
